title: CA AB2504: Community colleges: artificial intelligence: pilot program.

obligations: The chancellor's office shall establish the Future of Creative Industries Pilot Program (Sec. 78026.2(a)(1)).
The pilot program shall be developed in partnership with labor unions representing creative workers and with industry representatives (Sec. 78026.2(a)(2)).

The pilot program shall be developed to achieve the goals of supporting workers in California's creative and entertainment industries who have been or are at risk of being displaced by generative artificial intelligence, ensuring each participating community college program is designed and implemented in meaningful partnership with labor unions and industry representatives, and establishing a coordinated, outcomes driven model that can be replicated across sectors facing artificial intelligence driven employment disruption (Sec. 78026.2(a)(3)).
On or before June 30, 2027, the chancellor's office shall establish eligibility criteria for community colleges seeking to apply to participate in the pilot program (Sec. 78026.2(b)).

The pilot program shall be limited to up to 10 community colleges statewide, selected by the chancellor's office, and the chancellor's office is encouraged to ensure equitable access between the northern, central, and southern regions of the state (Sec. 78026.2(c)).
Implementation of the pilot program for the selected community colleges shall commence on or before July 1, 2028 (Sec. 78026.3).
On or before January 1, 2032, the chancellor's office shall submit a report to the Legislature evaluating the effectiveness of the pilot program at participating community colleges (Sec. 78026.4(a)).

The report shall include the number of participants who completed the pilot program, a comprehensive list of the certificates or degrees awarded to participants who completed the pilot program, and outcomes and job placement rates of participants who completed the pilot program, disaggregated by student demographics (Sec. 78026.4(b)).
The report shall include outcomes and legislative recommendations (Sec. 78026.4(c)).
The report shall be submitted in compliance with Section 9795 of the Government Code (Sec. 78026.4(d)).
This article shall become operative only upon an appropriation by the Legislature in the annual Budget Act or another statute for its purposes (Sec. 78026.5).
This article shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2033, and as of that date is repealed (Sec. 78026.6).
prohibitions: The pilot program shall be limited to up to 10 community colleges statewide (Sec. 78026.2(c)).

What it does

This law establishes the Future of Creative Industries Pilot Program within the California Community Colleges. The program supports workers in creative and entertainment industries who have been or are at risk of being displaced by generative artificial intelligence through reskilling and upskilling opportunities. It requires a report to the Legislature by January 1, 2032, and repeals the program on January 1, 2033.

Who it applies to

  • The chancellor's office of the California Community Colleges (Sec. 78026.1(a), 78026.2)
  • Up to 10 community colleges selected by the chancellor's office (Sec. 78026.2(c))
  • Workers in California's creative and entertainment industries who have been or are at risk of being displaced by generative artificial intelligence (Sec. 78026.2(a)(3)(A))
  • Labor unions representing creative workers and industry representatives as development partners (Sec. 78026.2(a)(2))

Effective date

This article becomes operative only upon an appropriation by the Legislature in the annual Budget Act or another statute for its purposes (Sec. 78026.5). Implementation for selected community colleges must commence on or before July 1, 2028 (Sec. 78026.3).

Key definitions

  • Chancellor's office: the office of the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges (Sec. 78026.1(a))
  • Future of Creative Industries Pilot Program or pilot program: the program established pursuant to Section 78026.2 (Sec. 78026.1(b))

Obligations

  • The chancellor's office shall establish the Future of Creative Industries Pilot Program (Sec. 78026.2(a)(1)).
  • The pilot program shall be developed in partnership with labor unions representing creative workers and with industry representatives (Sec. 78026.2(a)(2)).
  • The pilot program shall be developed to achieve the goals of supporting workers in California's creative and entertainment industries who have been or are at risk of being displaced by generative artificial intelligence, ensuring each participating community college program is designed and implemented in meaningful partnership with labor unions and industry representatives, and establishing a coordinated, outcomes driven model that can be replicated across sectors facing artificial intelligence driven employment disruption (Sec. 78026.2(a)(3)).
  • On or before June 30, 2027, the chancellor's office shall establish eligibility criteria for community colleges seeking to apply to participate in the pilot program (Sec. 78026.2(b)).
  • The pilot program shall be limited to up to 10 community colleges statewide, selected by the chancellor's office, and the chancellor's office is encouraged to ensure equitable access between the northern, central, and southern regions of the state (Sec. 78026.2(c)).
  • Implementation of the pilot program for the selected community colleges shall commence on or before July 1, 2028 (Sec. 78026.3).
  • On or before January 1, 2032, the chancellor's office shall submit a report to the Legislature evaluating the effectiveness of the pilot program at participating community colleges (Sec. 78026.4(a)).
  • The report shall include the number of participants who completed the pilot program, a comprehensive list of the certificates or degrees awarded to participants who completed the pilot program, and outcomes and job placement rates of participants who completed the pilot program, disaggregated by student demographics (Sec. 78026.4(b)).
  • The report shall include outcomes and legislative recommendations (Sec. 78026.4(c)).
  • The report shall be submitted in compliance with Section 9795 of the Government Code (Sec. 78026.4(d)).
  • This article shall become operative only upon an appropriation by the Legislature in the annual Budget Act or another statute for its purposes (Sec. 78026.5).
  • This article shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2033, and as of that date is repealed (Sec. 78026.6).

Prohibitions

  • The pilot program shall be limited to up to 10 community colleges statewide (Sec. 78026.2(c)).

Penalties and enforcement

The text does not state any enforcement authority, penalties, or private right of action. The chancellor's office is required to submit a report to the Legislature (Sec. 78026.4).

How it affects AI deployment

  • The statute does not impose direct obligations on organisations deploying artificial intelligence; it creates a community college pilot program to reskill and upskill workers in creative and entertainment industries who have been or are at risk of being displaced by generative artificial intelligence (Sec. 78026.2(a)(3)(A)).
  • Organisations in creative industries may be involved as industry representatives in developing the pilot program, including curriculum and training models (Sec. 78026.2(a)(2), (a)(3)(B)).
  • The pilot program is limited to up to 10 community colleges and requires partnership with labor unions and industry representatives, so an organisation deploying artificial intelligence in creative industries could participate as an industry representative if selected (Sec. 78026.2(a)(2), (c)).

Notable exemptions

  • No exemptions are stated in the text.

Compliance steps

  • The chancellor's office establishes the Future of Creative Industries Pilot Program (Sec. 78026.2(a)(1)).
  • Develop the pilot program in partnership with labor unions representing creative workers and with industry representatives (Sec. 78026.2(a)(2)).
  • Ensure the pilot program achieves the three goals, including supporting workers displaced by generative artificial intelligence and ensuring partnership in curriculum and training models (Sec. 78026.2(a)(3)).
  • On or before June 30, 2027, establish eligibility criteria for community colleges seeking to apply (Sec. 78026.2(b)).
  • Select up to 10 community colleges statewide, with equitable access across northern, central, and southern regions encouraged (Sec. 78026.2(c)).
  • Commence implementation for selected community colleges on or before July 1, 2028 (Sec. 78026.3).
  • On or before January 1, 2032, submit a report to the Legislature evaluating effectiveness, including participant completion numbers, certificates or degrees awarded, outcomes and job placement rates disaggregated by demographics, and legislative recommendations, in compliance with Government Code Section 9795 (Sec. 78026.4).
  • Ensure the article is operative only upon appropriation and ceases to be in effect on January 1, 2033 (Sec. 78026.5, 78026.6).

 Assembly Bill
 No. 2504 Introduced by Assembly Member Bauer-Kahan (Coauthors: Assembly Members Petrie-Norris, Michelle Rodriguez, and Sharp-Collins) February 20, 2026 An act to add and repeal Article 1.7 (commencing with Section 78026) of Chapter 1 of Part 48 of Division 7 of Title 3 of the Education Code, relating to community colleges. LEGISLATIVE COUNSEL'S DIGEST AB 2504, Bauer-Kahan.
 Community colleges: artificial intelligence: pilot program. Existing law establishes the California Community Colleges, administered by the Board of Governors of the California Community Colleges, as one of the segments of public postsecondary education in the state. Existing law requires the board to appoint a chief executive officer, known as the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges. Existing law establishes community college districts throughout the state, under the administration of community college district governing boards, and authorizes these districts to provide instruction at the community college campuses they operate. This bill, upon appropriation, would require the chancellor’s office to implement the Future of Creative Industries Pilot Program, commencing on or before July 1, 2028, and to select up to 10 community
 colleges to participate in the pilot program, as specified. The bill would require the chancellor’s office, on or before January 1, 2032, to submit a report to the Legislature evaluating the effectiveness of the pilot program, as provided. The bill would repeal this pilot program on January 1, 2033. Digest Key

 NO    Bill Text The people of the State of California do enact as follows: SECTION 1.  Article 1.7 (commencing with Section 78026) is added to Chapter 1 of Part 48 of Division 7 of Title 3 of the Education Code, to read: 
 Article
  1.7. Future of Creative Industries Pilot Program 78026.  This article shall be known, and may be cited, as the Future of Creative Industries Pilot Program. 78026.1.  For purposes of this article, the following definitions apply: (a) “Chancellor’s office” means the office of the Chancellor of the California Community Colleges. (b) “Future of Creative Industries Pilot Program” or “pilot program” means the program established pursuant to Section 78026.2. 78026.2.  (a) (1) The chancellor’s office shall establish the Future of Creative Industries Pilot Program. (2) The pilot program shall be developed in partnership with labor unions representing creative workers and with industry representatives. (3) The pilot program shall be developed to achieve all of the following goals: (A) Supporting workers in California’s creative and entertainment industries, including film, television, music, touring, and live events, who have been or are at risk of being displaced by generative
 artificial intelligence, including sound engineers, voice actors, concept artists, and employees in entry-level positions, by providing structured reskilling and upskilling opportunities through the California Community Colleges. (B) Ensuring that each participating community college program is designed and implemented in meaningful partnership with labor unions representing creative workers and with industry representatives so that curriculum and training models reflect the real tools, conditions, and career pathways of the workforce being served. (C) Establishing a coordinated, outcomes-driven model that California Community Colleges and workforce systems can replicate across sectors facing
 artificial intelligence-driven employment disruption. (b) On or before June 30, 2027, the chancellor’s office shall establish eligibility criteria for community colleges seeking to apply to participate in the pilot program. (c) The pilot program shall be limited to up to 10 community colleges statewide, to be selected by the chancellor’s office. In selecting community colleges for participation in the pilot
 program, the chancellor’s office is encouraged to ensure that there is equitable access to the pilot program between the northern, central, and southern regions of the state. 78026.3.  Implementation of the pilot program for the selected community colleges shall commence on or before July 1, 2028. 78026.4.  (a) On or before January 1, 2032, the chancellor’s office shall submit a report to the Legislature evaluating the effectiveness of the pilot program at community colleges participating in the pilot program. (b) (1) The report submitted pursuant to subdivision (a) shall include, but not be limited to, the number of participants who completed the pilot program, a
 comprehensive list of the certificates or degrees awarded to participants who completed the pilot program, and outcomes and job placement rates of participants who completed the pilot program. (2) The data described in paragraph (1) shall be disaggregated by student demographics. (c) The report submitted pursuant to subdivision (a) shall include outcomes and legislative recommendations. (d) The report submitted pursuant to subdivision (a) shall be submitted in compliance with Section 9795 of the Government Code. 78026.5.  This article shall become operative only upon an appropriation by the Legislature in the annual Budget Act or another statute for its purposes. 78026.6.  This article shall remain in effect only until January 1, 2033, and as of that date is repealed.
